summary: Section 4 and Table 1 give the plates, volumes, inoculation scheme, instrument settings and the screening concentration for each of the 18 compounds. The gaps left (medium formulation, stock solvents, run length, robot handling parameters, plate sterilisation, blank and plate-map layout) are either resolved from manufacturer pages or have defensible standard defaults. None of them would change what the growth assay measures.

gaps.detail: Screening concentration of each of the 18 antimicrobials (and WT MIC)
gaps.why_needed: The sub-inhibitory dose defines the assay condition. It is not stated in the Methods text.
gaps.resolution: Table 1 (mg/L, MIC → screen): azithromycin 30→7.5; cefiderocol 1→0.25; cefoperazone 0.5→0.25; chloramphenicol 2.5→1.25; ceftriaxone 2.5→1; D-cycloserine 12.5→6.25; flumequine >1.5→1.5; gentamicin 4→2; levofloxacin 0.25→0.125; meropenem 0.0625→0.03125; ofloxacin 0.125→0.0625; ornidazole 800→400; paraquat >268→67; fosfomycin 50→25; rifampicin 25→12.5; streptomycin 25→6.25; trimethoprim 2.3→0.25; zidovudine >100→100. Two figure legends disagree with Table 1: Fig 6 says 400 mg/L azithromycin (text and table say 7.5) and Fig 7 says 32 mg/L paraquat (text and table say 67). Use the Table 1 values.

gaps.why_needed: The medium composition affects growth and drug activity.
gaps.resolution: The paper names the medium only as LB. Assume standard Lennox LB: 10 g/L tryptone, 5 g/L yeast extract, 5 g/L NaCl, autoclaved, no supplements.

gaps.detail: Antibiotic stock preparation (solvent, stock concentration, sterilisation, storage)
gaps.why_needed: Needed to make LB containing each antibiotic at the Table 1 dose.
gaps.resolution: The paper says only that compounds were 'readily soluble in our LB media'. Assume stocks are made fresh in water, or the minimum DMSO/ethanol needed for poorly soluble compounds (e.g. rifampicin, azithromycin, flumequine). Filter-sterilise, then dilute into LB so the final solvent is ≤1% v/v. Include a matching solvent control if a solvent is used. Make one bulk antibiotic-LB per compound for all 5 plates × 2 replicates.

gaps.detail: Overnight pre-culture conditions (shaking speed, duration, deep-well plate type, inoculum from glycerol stock) and cell density of the stored droplet
gaps.why_needed: The starting inoculum comes from the 1:1 culture:50% glycerol mix. Its density sets the lag phase and AUC.
gaps.resolution: Paper: 1 mL LB per well in a deep-well plate, inoculated from glycerol stocks, grown overnight at 37 °C with agitation. Then mix with 1 mL 50% glycerol (about 25% glycerol final). Assume 16–20 h at about 220–250 rpm, with the culture reaching stationary phase. Dispense 3 µL of the mix into each CR1496c well, giving about 1:100 dilution of the 0.5× culture on adding 297 µL. Store at −20 °C for up to 3 weeks, or at −80 °C for longer. OD was not measured or normalised in the paper.
gaps.source: Section 4 of the paper; standard practice for the unstated parts

gaps.detail: Plate layout / strain map, WT and blank wells, replicate placement
gaps.why_needed: Each of the 5 plates holds the 447 knockouts plus WT. The G-value→OD600 conversion needs blank wells (G_blank), and the knockouts need to be identified. Plate maps are not in the text.
gaps.resolution: Use the 5-plate library layout (447 Keio transporter knockouts plus BW1556 WT; see refs 19 and 20). Include at least one uninoculated medium well per plate for G_blank, and WT wells on every plate. Run duplicates as a second full set (10 plates on the Growth Profiler 960). Record the map so wells can be matched to strains. Missed-inoculation wells show as no growth in one replicate only and are excluded.

gaps.detail: Run duration of the Growth Profiler assay
gaps.why_needed: The AUC and max OD depend on the time window.
gaps.resolution: Not stated for the screen. The MIC was read at 48 h, so run for 48 h with images every 20 min (about 145 time points) at 37 °C and 225 rpm.
gaps.source: Section 2.2 (48 h MIC readout) and Section 4

gaps.detail: Growth Profiler 960 settings and OD conversion
gaps.resolution: Paper: 37 °C, 225 rpm, image every 20 min. OD600 = 0.0158 × (G − G_blank)^0.9854. Manufacturer: CR1496c is a 96-half-deepwell polystyrene plate with a 0.3 mL recommended culture volume, sterilised by gamma irradiation and single use. Typical shaking is 225 rpm at 50 mm. The CR1396b cover has 0.8 mm holes and an evaporation rate of 8 µL/well/day at 30 °C and 50% humidity. Enzyscreen's strain-calibration page describes a green-value→OD calibration run at 250 rpm with a dilution series; the paper's a and b values replace the need to repeat it.

gaps.detail: Plate and cover sterilisation 'by washing and UV in accordance with manufacturer instructions' (deferred method)
gaps.why_needed: Needed for sterility and to avoid cross-contamination between runs.
gaps.resolution: The manufacturer lists CR1496c as single use and non-autoclavable, and I found no washing or UV procedure for the polystyrene plates. The assay result does not depend on how plates are re-sterilised, so use fresh gamma-sterilised CR1496c plates. If plates are reused, wash thoroughly, rinse with water, and UV-treat in a biosafety cabinet. Covers CR1396b are autoclavable: wrap and autoclave 20–30 min at 120 °C with a dry cycle (or oven-dry about 1 h at 100–110 °C), or wipe the seal with a water–ethanol mixture. Do not use a dishwasher.

gaps.detail: Opentrons OT-2 liquid-handling parameters (deferred to scripts on GitHub, which were deliberately not consulted)
gaps.why_needed: Needed to reproduce dispensing of 3 µL droplets and 297 µL antibiotic-LB.
gaps.resolution: The text gives the volumes and tools: 3 µL culture:glycerol mix per well with the 20 µL multichannel, and 297 µL LB plus antibiotic per well with the 300 µL multichannel. Assume a fresh tip per column or reservoir fill, dispensing at the well bottom into or onto the droplet at default OT-2 flow rates. For the 3 µL droplet, touch the tip to the well bottom so the droplet is deposited. Add the LB with a gentle dispense, no mixing, then seal with the CR1396b cover straight away. Assume the plates are thawed at room temperature, or the LB is added to the frozen droplet; the paper does not say which.
gaps.source: standard practice; Section 4 of the paper

gaps.detail: Wild-type MIC determination method (inoculum and dilution range)
gaps.why_needed: Needed only if the doses are re-derived; the final screening doses are already in Table 1.
gaps.resolution: Not needed to run the screen, since Table 1 gives the doses. If MICs are to be repeated: use a two-fold dilution series in LB with BW1556 and read OD at 48 h. MIC is the lowest concentration giving <10% of the antibiotic-free OD. Assume the same 3 µL inoculation format.

retrieved_details: From the paper (https://www.mdpi.com/2079-6382/11/8/1129): Table 1 screening concentrations in mg/L: azithromycin 7.5, cefiderocol 0.25, cefoperazone 0.25, chloramphenicol 1.25, ceftriaxone 1, D-cycloserine 6.25, flumequine 1.5, gentamicin 2, levofloxacin 0.125, meropenem 0.03125, ofloxacin 0.0625, ornidazole 400, paraquat 67, fosfomycin 25, rifampicin 12.5, streptomycin 6.25, trimethoprim 0.25, zidovudine 100. WT MICs are 30, 1, 0.5, 2.5, 2.5, 12.5, >1.5, 4, 0.25, 0.0625, 0.125, 800, >268, 50, 25, 25, 2.3 and >100 mg/L respectively. The Fig 6 legend (400 mg/L azithromycin) and Fig 7 legend (32 mg/L paraquat) conflict with the text and table. Use the table values. The mean baseline AUC in LB was about 30.0 and the max growth rate about 1.19 per h. Wild type is E. coli BW1556, the Keio parent. Sigma supplied the antibiotics except rifampicin, ceftriaxone and azithromycin, which came from TCI. Library: 447 transporter knockouts over 5 plates, run in duplicate. Overall workflow: overnight 1 mL LB culture in a deep-well plate at 37 °C; add 1 mL 50% glycerol; put 3 µL into each well of a CR1496c plate; store at −20 °C (≤3 weeks) or −80 °C; start the assay by adding 297 µL antibiotic-LB, seal with a CR1396b cover; run in the Growth Profiler 960 at 37 °C, 225 rpm, imaging every 20 min. Convert G-values with OD600 = 0.0158 × (G − G_blank)^0.9854. Manufacturer data (Enzyscreen): CR1496c is polystyrene, single use and not autoclavable, with 8×8 mm square wells 17 mm deep, 1.1 mL per well, 0.3 mL recommended culture volume, gamma-sterilised (https://www.enzyscreen.com/product/polystyrene-transparent-square-96-half-deepwell-microplates-CR1496c/). CR1396b: 0.8 mm holes, headspace air exchange 0.3 mL/min, evaporation 8 µL/well/day at 30 °C and 50% humidity, autoclavable and reusable (https://www.enzyscreen.com/product/universal-sandwich-cover-for-96-well-mtps-stackable/). Cover maintenance: autoclave 20–30 min at 120 °C wrapped, dry cycle or oven 100–110 °C for 1 h, wipe seal with a water–ethanol mixture, no dishwasher (https://www.enzyscreen.com/article/maintenance-sterilisation-and-use-of-sandwich-covers/). Growth Profiler calibration instructions (green value→OD; run at 250 rpm, 2-min interval) are at https://www.enzyscreen.com/strain-calibration/. Standard Lennox LB: 10 g/L tryptone, 5 g/L yeast extract, 5 g/L NaCl (https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sigma/l3022). The paper's GitHub scripts and supplementary files were not used.
